title: API Quickstart & Developer Pricing Messaging (sketch)
content:
Summary:

This is a working sketch for developer-facing messaging and pricing language for Redwood's Hosted API. Goal: craft short quickstart hooks and clear pricing phrasing that emphasizes developer velocity, predictable performance, and transparent unit economics. This doc is intentionally tactical — quick headline variants, a 5-minute quickstart angle, sample SDK-first copy, and a set of pricing blurbs we can A/B test on the product page and sign-up flows.

Headline / hero copy options (short):
- "Redwood Hosted API — production LLMs that feel like a native SDK"
- "Ship LLM features fast: predictable latency, transparent cost, zero ops"
- "Start in minutes. Scale without surprise bills."

One-liner elevator (3 variants):
1) "A developer-first API for text, chat and embeddings with predictable latency and usage-based pricing that scales from prototype to production."
2) "Secure, high-throughput LLM inference with simple SDKs, streaming responses, and clear per-token pricing."
3) "Redwood Hosted API: fast to start, predictable to run — built for engineers shipping LLM features."

Key developer value props (short bullets for use on landing, quickstart pages):
- "Start in 5 minutes: SDKs, examples, and pre-made templates for chat, summarization, and embeddings."
- "Predictable performance: latency SLOs and model profiles so you know what to expect in production."
- "Transparent unit economics: per-token pricing, cost-breakdowns in the Console, and recommended batching settings."
- "No ops: managed model hosting with automatic routing and fallback to compatible variants."
- "Secure by default: API keys, org-level roles, and optional VPC/private deployments for regulated data."

Quickstart angles (copy + flows to test):
1) Minimal friction (5-minute flow)
- Hook: "Invite, paste an API key, run the sample curl."
- Steps: create org (or sign-in), get free credits, pick "Chat quickstart", paste sample request into terminal, view live stream in Console.
- Example snippet (web-friendly, one-line curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-clarity-7b","input":"Summarize this email in two bullets"}'
- Messaging: "No infra. No model downloads. Real responses in seconds."

2) SDK-first (Node / Python)
- Hook: "Use the SDK you already know; upgrade later without rewriting code."
- Example Node flow: install package, one function call to create stream, handle tokens.
- Messaging: "We handle batching, kv-caching, and streaming so your event loop stays happy."

3) Template-led onboarding (PLG friendly)
- Hook: pick a template (QA bot, inbox summarizer, semantic search) and click "Deploy demo" to get a pre-wired example that includes prompts, eval prompts, and a small test dataset.
- Messaging: "From template to working demo in 60 seconds — then customize prompts and model version."

Pricing-language drafts (to A/B and validate with legal/finance):
- Core principles to communicate: simple units, transparent math, and predictable controls.
- Suggested header copy: "Pay only for what you use. Clear per-token pricing with committed discounts and reserved capacity for predictable workloads."

Short copy snippets (landing page / pricing panel):
- "Per-token billing for generation and embeddings — no hidden multipliers."
- "Free tier: 2M tokens / month for testing and early development (auto-expire after 90 days of inactivity)."
- "Volume discounts: automatic breaks at 50M / 200M / 1B tokens; committed plans available for Dedicated/Private."
- "Burst and safety: burst traffic allowed within quota; overages paused and surfaced in Console before billing when possible."

Example pricing paragraph (developer-facing):
"Generation: $0.003 / 1,000 tokens (rwd-clarity-7b); Embeddings: $0.0006 / vector. Usage shown in Console with token-by-token breakdown and a recommended batching guide. Commitments and reserved capacity available for teams who need predictable monthly spend — contact sales for custom SLAs and private deployments."

Pricing microcopy suggestions (CTA for cost control):
- "Set a monthly cap to avoid surprises"
- "Try our optimizer: one-click batching and cache suggestions to reduce token spend by up to X%"
- "See estimated cost for this request" (inline estimator next to SDK playground)

Competitive positioning notes (short analysis to use in battlecards):
- Vs cloud provider endpoints (AWS/GCP):
  - Redwood advantage: curated model catalog and runtime optimizations (KV cache, batching), developer ergonomics (templates + SDKs) and transparent latency profiles.
  - Typical cloud pitch: broader infra services and deeper enterprise integrations — rebuttal: we integrate with their infra, but provide a higher-level inference runtime that reduces engineering time-to-value.
- Vs LLM API players (simplicity-first vendors):
  - Redwood advantage: predictable performance, explicit cost controls, and paths to dedicated/private deployments for regulated customers.
  - Tradeoff: slightly more configuration for advanced performance tuning — but that yields measurable cost/latency gains.
- Vs self-hosted inference stacks:
  - Redwood advantage: no infra ops, maintenance, or perf regressions to track. Offer private deployments when customers insist on full control.

Target personas and tailored hooks:
- Product/feature engineers: "Start with a template, ship a 1-click demo to PMs."
- ML engineers: "Tune model variants, deploy canary traffic, and inspect KV-hit rates in the Console."
- Platform teams: "Reserve capacity and enforce org-level quotas with audit logs and KMS integration."

Objections and quick rebuttals (for sales enablement):
- "We can host ourselves": "Self-hosting moves cost and complexity to your team. Redwood offers the same kernel-level optimizations plus observability and rollout tooling — we also offer Private if you need on-prem control."
- "Pricing is opaque": "We expose token breakdowns, per-request estimators, and cost recommendations in the Console. Default settings include sensible caps and alerts."
- "Latency varies by model": "We publish model performance profiles and support routing/fallbacks so you can enforce SLOs in production."

Suggested experiments (quick A/B tests):
1) Hero CTA A: "Start free — 2M tokens" vs CTA B: "Run a live demo in your browser" (measure signups -> project creation)
2) Pricing page microcopy: show 'estimated cost for 1k tokens' inline vs hidden estimator (measure time-on-page & conversion)
3) Quickstart flow: template-first vs SDK-first (measure success -> deploy demo)

Next steps / owners:
- Validate pricing numbers with finance (owner: Priya) — target: finalize per-token rates for public pricing by EOW.
- Implement inline cost estimator in SDK playground (owner: Ethan) — prototype by next sprint.
- Create 3 quickstart templates (chat, embeddings search, summarizer) and wire 'Deploy demo' flow (owner: Carlos) — ship as beta for PLG cohort.

Notes / open questions:
- Free tier size & renewal policy: propose 2M tokens with 90 days of inactivity expiry; finance to confirm.
- Should we show model-specific price multipliers for quantized variants? (ops & finance tradeoff).
- Messaging test: "production-first API" vs "developer-first API" — which resonates more at top of funnel?

This doc is a working draft for product marketing, growth, and sales enablement — please push edits directly in this file, tag the associated linked artifacts, and drop examples of the quickstart flows you want to ship.
